text:
Asha M.: :wave: Drafted a compact SLO/SLA section for the launch PRD. Primary ask: agree on fallback modes + clear acceptance criteria so engineering can scope gated rollouts. Link: https://redwood.internal/prd/slo-launch-draft — please review by EOD and flag anything that would block launch.

Mike L.: skimmed it. main question: do we treat embeddings/generation differently for error budgets? embeddings can be best-effort for some customers. want concrete numbers we can code into the router.

Sara S.: agree. provisional proposal:
- critical routes (customer-facing chat, sync inference): p95 latency <= 300ms, error budget 0.1% per day
- non-critical async/embeddings: p95 <= 800ms, error budget 0.5% per day
- graceful degrade tiers: quantized same-model -> smaller model variant -> cached response -> rate-limit fallback.
Will add acceptance test vectors for each tier.

Jon P.: for model-switch fallback we need an eval acceptance threshold. suggestion: automated eval set; request-level quality metric drop <= 2 pts (ROUGE/ATTN-sim) and no catastrophic hallucination (score on hallucination-detector < 0.02). If a fallback violates that, we should fail open to dedicated capacity or block rollout.

Leah C.: customers we've spoken to (FinCorp, HealthCo) want an enterprise SLA: guaranteed p95 <= 250ms and 99.9% availability, else credit. They expect dedicated capacity fallback rather than model degradation. we should surface that as a paid-tier option in the PRD.

Mike L.: implementation plan sketch: router policy ordered by latency/cost budget + customer tier. sample config: 
```json
{
  "fallback_policy": [
    {"type":"quantize","max_latency_ms":500},
    {"type":"model_switch","target":"redwood-std-6B","max_latency_ms":800},
    {"type":"cache","ttl_ms":60000},
    {"type":"rate_limit","concurrency":10}
  ]
}
```
This gives SRE something concrete to enforce and product something to sell.

Sara S.: acceptance criteria that engineering can test:
- failover correctness: verified in staging with synthetic traffic (simulate 2x expected peak)
- observable metrics: fallback_count, fallback_latency_ms, quality_regressions by eval-set id
- automated rollback triggers: 3 rule hits within 10m -> rollback to previous model or divert to dedicated pool
I'll draft the canary gating rules based on that.

Asha M.: nice. need to prioritize which fallbacks ship in v1. Proposal: v1 minimal: quantize + model_switch + cache. rate limiting and dedicated-pool routing for enterprise as v1+. Thoughts?

Leah C.: that aligns with customer asks. flagging HealthCo — they'd pay for dedicated routing in v1+.

Jon P.: v1 minimal is fine but lock in the eval harness and threshold. we can't iterate on quality after launch without that baseline.

Mike L.: engineering estimate: quantize + model_switch + cache = 3 sprint work for runtime + 1 sprint for tests/observability. rate-limit/dedicated-routing additional 2 sprints.

Asha M.: thanks everyone — please drop comments in the PRD doc rather than long threads.
